question: May `socket.drain` intentionally close slow subscribers to prioritize teardown signaling, or must it preserve the existing connection and backpressure behavior?
rationale: This choice changes the public Gateway compatibility and availability contract, which source inspection and responsive-client proof cannot safely decide without owner intent.

options.title: Preserve connections
options.body: Keep the existing best-effort slow-client behavior and implement drain delivery through a bounded compatible path.

options.title: Close slow clients
options.body: Approve disconnect-on-drain, document it as protocol behavior, and require saturated-buffer and client-recovery proof.

options.title: Defer the event
options.body: Pause the feature until a reliable bounded delivery contract can be defined.

recommendation.title: Preserve connections
recommendation.body: Keep the existing best-effort slow-client behavior and implement drain delivery through a bounded compatible path.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle introduced the current slow-consumer behavior and has the strongest recent ownership signal for the Gateway broadcaster contract.
